title: Doc Cheatham
summary: Cheatham played five or six years in Bauza's band; he admired his lyric style.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What about Doc Cheetam? He played with (inaudible) --
-- he played with Calloway, and then he --

He play (inaudible) in my band. He stay with my band about five, six years, play well. He's a hell of a Dixieland man. He's one of the best left. He was -- I used to admire Cheetam -- I used to hear Cheetam in the record. I told you about McKinley's Cottonpickers. He was the first trumpet player in that band. He used to play songs in that band. (Inaudible) trumpet, play those -- he played a style, semi-Swiss style, like a big (inaudible) all round that way (inaudible) play the melody, beautiful phrase with a nice link here and there and so forth. You know what I mean? They didn't play the hard jazz. They played the other thing.
Yeah. Yeah. (Inaudible) playing beautiful. Well, he (inaudible) big (inaudible) group, go on Broadway (inaudible) Dixieland (inaudible). He's big now, big now as he can be.
